```text
// Mutation testing for Sprint 3 (D6). Run it on the files your PR changed, never on the whole repo:
//   TZ=UTC yarn stryker run --mutate "path/to/file.ts"
// Set STRYKER_JSON to write the JSON report where the course wants it, for example
//   STRYKER_JSON=docs/sprint3/mutation/reports/130-zach-short-before.json
/** @type {import("@stryker-mutator/api/core").PartialStrykerOptions} */
export default {
  testRunner: "vitest",
  plugins: ["@stryker-mutator/vitest-runner"],
  vitest: {
    configFile: "vitest.config.mts",
    // Only the tests that import the mutated file run, which keeps a run to minutes in this monorepo.
    related: true,
  },
  // Not inPlace: in this repo the in-place backup lands inside the project, Vitest then collects the backup
  // copies, and the restore drops the executable bit on scripts. The sandbox copy avoids both. These folders
  // have no unit tests that features or web code import, so leaving them out keeps the copy small.
  // .claude and .cursor hold symlinks to folders, and packages/prisma/.env links to a root .env that may not
  // exist; the sandbox copy fails on all three.
  ignorePatterns: [
    "docs",
    "ai-logs",
    "specs",
    "apps/api/v2",
    "apps/web/public",
    "packages/embeds",
    "reports",
    ".claude",
    ".cursor",
    "packages/prisma/.env",
  ],
  ignoreStatic: true,
  concurrency: 4,
  timeoutMS: 30000,
  reporters: ["clear-text", "progress", "json", "html"],
  jsonReporter: { fileName: process.env.STRYKER_JSON ?? "reports/mutation/mutation.json" },
  htmlReporter: { fileName: "reports/mutation/mutation.html" },
};
```

```text
# Mutation testing: Issue #138 -- Allow hosts to confirm or reject individual recurring booking occurrences

**PR(s):** [#140](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/cal.diy/pull/140)  **Tool:** StrykerJS 10.1.1 with the Vitest runner  **Config:** [stryker.138.config.mjs](../../../stryker.138.config.mjs) + [vitest.stryker-138.config.mts](../../../vitest.stryker-138.config.mts), built on the shared [stryker.config.mjs](../../../stryker.config.mjs) by @zach-short  **Command:** `STRYKER_JSON=docs/sprint3/mutation/reports/138-zachbowden-<before|after>.json TZ=UTC nvm exec 22 node_modules/.bin/stryker run stryker.138.config.mjs`
**Reports:** [before](reports/138-zachbowden-before.json) · [after](reports/138-zachbowden-after.json)
**Mutation score:** before 50.60% → after 81.71% (covered mutants only: 73.68% → 97.10%)

### Setup notes

- **Only the lines this PR added or changed are mutated.** `stryker.138.config.mjs` lists them as line ranges: the new guard in `confirm.handler.ts`, `findByRecurringEventId` in `BookingRepository.ts`, the new lines in `BookingListItem.tsx`, and all of `ManageOccurrencesDialog.tsx` and the two `getRecurringOccurrences` files.
- **The test list is explicit.** `vitest.stryker-138.config.mts` names this PR's test files plus `BookingRepository.test.ts`. The shared config's `related: true` would also run every test that imports `BookingRepository`, including unrelated calendar-subscription suites that time out under load. A failure on the unmutated code stops Stryker before it mutates anything.
- **Stryker 10 requires Node 22 or newer;** the machine's default is Node 20, so the run uses `nvm exec 22`.
- **Same mutants in both runs.** Both runs produced 99 mutants at identical locations, so the reports compare one-to-one.

| Status | Before | After |
|---|---|---|
| Killed | 42 | 67 |
| Survived | 15 | 2 |
| No coverage | 26 | 13 |
| Ignored (static) | 16 | 17 |

## Surviving mutants

All 15 survivors from the before report are in lines this PR added.

| Location (file:line) | Mutation | Equivalent or test gap? | Why |
|---|---|---|---|
| `confirm.handler.ts:187` | `if (!recurringEventId)` → `if (true)` | Test gap (killed after) | The new pending/not-ended guard is meant only for single-booking requests. No test sent a bulk request whose first booking fails the guard, so applying it to bulk requests went unnoticed. Under the mutant, "Confirm all" on a series whose first booking has ended would be refused. The issue (Q2) says the bulk behaviour must not change. |
| `confirm.handler.ts:191` | status error message → empty | Test gap (killed after) | Tests checked only `code: "BAD_REQUEST"`. API v2 and email-link callers get this message as their only explanation. The project's error-handling rule requires errors that name the record and the reason. |
| `confirm.handler.ts:194` | `endTime < now` → `endTime <= now` | Equivalent | Only differs when the booking ends at exactly the current millisecond. The AC says "past" without defining that instant, and no test can reliably create that state. |
| `confirm.handler.ts:197` | "already ended" message → empty | Test gap (killed after) | Same as line 191. |
| `getRecurringOccurrences.handler.ts:23` | FORBIDDEN message → empty | Test gap (killed after) | Only the error code was asserted. |
| `getRecurringOccurrences.handler.ts:29` | `booking?.recurringEventId` → `booking.recurringEventId` | Test gap (killed after) | No test for a booking id that does not exist. Under the mutant, the query throws a `TypeError` (shown as a 500 error) instead of `BAD_REQUEST`. |

**Mutants with no coverage** (not survivors, but they count against the score):
- **`BookingRepository.ts:685-689`, `findByRecurringEventId` (11 mutants).** The handler test mocks the repository, so the method never ran in any test. A new repository test killed all 11.
- **`ManageOccurrencesDialog.tsx:57`, loading text.** No test rendered the loading state. Killed after.
- **`getRecurringOccurrences.schema.ts:7`, the Zod schema.** No test imported it. The new schema test runs it, but the schema is built when the module first loads, and `ignoreStatic` is on (from the shared config), so the after report lists it as **Ignored** rather than Killed. The new test still checks the schema rejects `{}`, `1.5` and `"5"`.
- **`BookingListItem.tsx:171-172`, `473-483` (13 mutants), still uncovered.** These lines decide when to show the "Manage occurrences" button and open the dialog. No unit test renders a booking row, because the row needs the data-table, actions-store and details-sheet providers. AC1's button placement was checked manually (see PR #140's Test Evidence), but this is still a gap in the automated tests.

## New or strengthened test

Commit: [PR #140](https://github.com/CSCI-435-SE/cal.diy/pull/140/files) · Test: `packages/trpc/server/routers/viewer/bookings/confirm.handler.individual.test.ts` › keeps Confirm all working when the series' first booking has already ended · Kills: `confirm.handler.ts:187` (`if (true)`)

The same change added or strengthened these tests, each killing the mutants listed (all show as Killed in the after report):

| Test | Kills |
|---|---|
| `confirm.handler.individual.test.ts` › refuses to act on a REJECTED / CANCELLED occurrence; refuses to act on an occurrence that has already ended (now also assert the message names the booking and the reason) | `confirm.handler.ts:191`, `:197` |
| `getRecurringOccurrences.handler.test.ts` › throws BAD_REQUEST when the booking does not exist | `getRecurringOccurrences.handler.ts:29` |
| `getRecurringOccurrences.handler.test.ts` › FORBIDDEN and not-recurring cases now also assert the message | `getRecurringOccurrences.handler.ts:23`, `:32` |
| `ManageOccurrencesDialog.test.tsx` › fetches this booking's series only while the dialog is open | `ManageOccurrencesDialog.tsx:42`, `:43` |
| `ManageOccurrencesDialog.test.tsx` › shows the translated title and description | `ManageOccurrencesDialog.tsx:51`, `:52` |
| `ManageOccurrencesDialog.test.tsx` › shows no rows when the query returns no data | `ManageOccurrencesDialog.tsx:60` |
| `ManageOccurrencesDialog.test.tsx` › shows each occurrence's date and time in the host's time zone and time format | `ManageOccurrencesDialog.tsx:74`, `:77` |
| `ManageOccurrencesDialog.test.tsx` › shows a loading message while the occurrences load | `ManageOccurrencesDialog.tsx:57` (was no coverage) |
| `BookingRepository.test.ts` › findByRecurringEventId returns the series' occurrences in chronological order with only the fields needed to act on them | `BookingRepository.ts:685-689` (11, were no coverage) |
| `getRecurringOccurrences.schema.test.ts` (new) | `getRecurringOccurrences.schema.ts:7` (now Ignored as static, see above) |

## Questions

**1. What did the surviving mutants reveal about your tests?**

My tests checked actions, not what the user or caller sees. The handler tests asserted the error code but never the message, which is all an API v2 or email-link caller gets. The dialog tests checked which buttons appear and what they send, but never the date and time AC1 requires, nor the title. Because those tests used dates relative to "now", they could not have asserted a formatted date anyway. The survivors also showed I had only tested the happy path. Nothing covered a booking that doesn't exist, a query with no data, or a bulk request whose first booking is in the past. That last one mattered most. My new guard was meant for single-booking requests, but no test would have caught it also blocking "Confirm all", which the issue says must not change. Finally, the 11 uncovered `BookingRepository` mutants showed that mocking the repository in the handler test meant the real query never ran in any test.

**2. Did any surviving mutant point to an assertion whose expected value was not based on the requirements? Explain.**

Not directly: the survivors came from missing assertions, not wrong expected values. They did force me to decide where some expected values come from. The ACs don't specify error wording, so the new message assertions don't copy the strings from the code. They only require that the message names the booking id and the reason (its status, or that it ended), which comes from the project's documented error-handling rule. For the date/time test, I worked out "Wed, 4 Mar 2099" and "10:00am - 10:15am" for 15:00 UTC in New York independently of the component. The date format matches the one the booking list already uses. The two boundary mutants (`<` vs `<=`, `>=` vs `>`) are the opposite case. The AC says "past" but doesn't define the exact ending instant, so no requirement gives an expected value. That's why I classified them as equivalent rather than adding a test pinned to my own choice.

**3. If you used AI to configure the tool, analyze survivors, or write tests, what did it produce and what did you verify or correct?**

I used Claude Code (log linked from PR #140).

- **Configuration:** it applied @zach-short's shared Stryker setup and wrote the issue-specific config. It mutates only this PR's changed line ranges and lists the test files explicitly, because `related: true` would also pull in calendar-subscription tests that time out.
- **Running:** the first run failed because Stryker 10 requires Node 22 and my machine had Node 20; I installed Node 22 with nvm and ran Stryker through it.
- **Analysis and tests:** it drafted the classification of the 15 survivors and the new tests.
- **What I verified:**
  - All 6 selected test files (36 tests) pass before mutation.
  - The before and after reports contain the same 99 mutants at the same locations.
  - Each "test gap" survivor shows as Killed in the after report.
  - The computed scores match Stryker's own summary table (81.71% / 97.10%).
- **What I corrected:** its first estimate counted the schema mutant as killed, but the after report shows it as Ignored (a static mutant with `ignoreStatic` on). This write-up reports it that way.
```

```text
  ...props

  const { t } = useLocale();

  // Two entries can touch, so a run of away slots is one panel only while the window stays the same. Slots of
  // a whole-day entry have no window, so they all compare equal.
  const inSamePanel = (slot: Slot, other: Slot | string | undefined) =>
    typeof other === "object" &&
    !!other.away &&
    other.outOfOfficeStart === slot.outOfOfficeStart &&
    other.outOfOfficeEnd === slot.outOfOfficeEnd;

  const oooAllDay = slots.length > 0 && slots.every((slot) => inSamePanel(slots[0], slot));
  if (oooAllDay) {
    return <OOOSlot {...slots[0]} />;
  }

  // A partial-day entry leaves a run of away slots in the middle of the day. One panel stands in for each run,
  // at the first away slot, so the panel sits between the slots before and after the window.

const OOOSlot: React.FC<IOOOSlotProps> = (props) => {
  const isPlatform = useIsPlatform();
  const { timeFormat, timezone } = useBookerTime();
  const { i18n } = useLocale();
  const { fromUser, toUser, reason, emoji, notes, showNotePublicly, time, className = "" } = props;
  const { outOfOfficeStart, outOfOfficeEnd } = props;

  if (isPlatform) return <></>;
  const awayWindow =
    outOfOfficeStart && outOfOfficeEnd
      ? formatAwayWindow(outOfOfficeStart, outOfOfficeEnd, timezone, timeFormat, i18n.language)
      : undefined;
  return (
    <OutOfOfficeInSlots
      fromUser={fromUser}
      toUser={toUser}
      date={dayjs(time).format("YYYY-MM-DD")}
      reason={reason}
      emoji={emoji}
      notes={notes}
      showNotePublicly={showNotePublicly}
      awayWindow={awayWindow}
      borderDashed
      className={className}
    />
```

```text
  const oooAllDay = slots.length > 0 && slots.every((slot) => inSamePanel(slots[0], slot));
  if (oooAllDay) {
    return <OOOSlot {...slots[0]} />;
  }

  // A partial-day entry leaves a run of away slots in the middle of the day. One panel stands in for each run,
  // at the first away slot, so the panel sits between the slots before and after the window.
  const merged = mergeByTime(slots, date ? bookedTimes : []);
  const items: ReactNode[] = [];
  for (let index = 0; index < merged.length; index++) {
    const slot = merged[index];
    if (typeof slot === "string") {
      items.push(
        <JoinWaitlistButton
          key={slot}
          date={date ?? ""}
          slotStart={slot}
          label={t("waitlist_join_time", { time: dayjs.utc(slot).tz(timezone).format(timeFormat) })}
        />
      );
      continue;
    }
    if (!slot.away) {
      items.push(<SlotItem key={slot.time} slot={slot} {...props} />);
      continue;
    }
    if (inSamePanel(slot, merged[index - 1])) continue;
    let runEnd = index;
    while (inSamePanel(slot, merged[runEnd + 1])) runEnd++;
    items.push(
      <OOOSlot key={`ooo-${slot.time}`} {...slot} className={runEnd === merged.length - 1 ? "pb-0" : ""} />
    );
```

```text
import { render } from "@calcom/features/bookings/Booker/__tests__/test-utils";
import type { Slots } from "@calcom/features/bookings/types";
import { fireEvent, screen, within } from "@testing-library/react";
import { afterEach, describe, expect, it, vi } from "vitest";
import { AvailableTimes } from "./AvailableTimes";

const push = vi.fn();
// What the attendee selected on the booking page. A test changes it to stand in another zone or format.
const bookerTime = vi.hoisted(() => ({ timeFormat: "HH:mm", timezone: "UTC" }));

vi.mock("next/navigation", async (importOriginal) => ({
  ...(await importOriginal<typeof import("next/navigation")>()),
  useRouter: () => ({ push }),
  useSearchParams: () => new URLSearchParams(),
  useParams: () => ({}),
  usePathname: () => "/host",
}));

vi.mock("@calcom/atoms/hooks/useIsPlatform", () => ({
  useIsPlatform: () => false,
}));

vi.mock("@calcom/features/bookings/Booker/hooks/useBookerTime", () => ({
  useBookerTime: () => bookerTime,
}));

vi.mock("@calcom/features/bookings/lib/useCheckOverlapWithOverlay", () => ({
  useCheckOverlapWithOverlay: () => ({
    isOverlapping: false,
    overlappingTimeStart: "",
    overlappingTimeEnd: "",
  }),
}));

vi.mock("@calcom/lib/hooks/useLocale", () => ({
  useLocale: () => ({
    t: (key: string, values?: { displayName?: string; start?: string; end?: string }) => {
      // The English string of `ooo_away_window`, as issue #130 words it.
      if (key === "ooo_away_window") return `Away ${values?.start} to ${values?.end}`;
      return values?.displayName ? `${key}:${values.displayName}` : key;
    },
    isLocaleReady: true,
    i18n: { language: "en" },
  }),
}));

type Slot = Slots[string][number];

const host = { fromUser: { id: 1, displayName: "Host" }, emoji: "🩺", showNotePublicly: false };

// 09:00 to 16:00 UTC on 2026-10-08, one slot an hour. The hours listed are away.
const dayWith = (awayHours: number[], awayData: Partial<Slot> = host): Slot[] =>
  Array.from({ length: 8 }, (_, index) => {
    const hour = 9 + index;
    const time = `2026-10-08T${String(hour).padStart(2, "0")}:00:00.000Z`;
    return awayHours.includes(hour) ? { time, away: true, ...awayData } : { time };
  });

const renderDay = (slots: Slot[]) => render(<AvailableTimes slots={slots} event={{ data: null }} />);

const windowOf = (start: string, end: string) => ({
  outOfOfficeStart: `2026-10-08T${start}:00.000Z`,
  outOfOfficeEnd: `2026-10-08T${end}:00.000Z`,
});

// Marks the slot that starts at `hour` UTC as away for the given entry.
const awayAt = (slots: Slot[], hour: number, awayData: Partial<Slot>): Slot[] =>
  slots.map((slot) =>
    Number(slot.time.slice(11, 13)) === hour ? { ...slot, away: true, ...awayData } : slot
  );

const panelOf = (text: string) => {
  const panel = screen.getByText(text).closest<HTMLElement>(".border-dashed");
  if (!panel) throw new Error(`No away panel holds "${text}"`);
  return panel;
};

const isBefore = (first: HTMLElement, second: HTMLElement) =>
  !!(first.compareDocumentPosition(second) & Node.DOCUMENT_POSITION_FOLLOWING);

// The hours of the slot buttons that come before and after the panel in document order.
const hoursAround = (panel: HTMLElement) => {
  const hourOf = (button: HTMLElement) => Number(button.dataset.time?.slice(11, 13));
  const buttons = screen.getAllByTestId("time");
  return {
    before: buttons
      .filter((button) => button.compareDocumentPosition(panel) & Node.DOCUMENT_POSITION_FOLLOWING)
      .map(hourOf),
    after: buttons
      .filter((button) => button.compareDocumentPosition(panel) & Node.DOCUMENT_POSITION_PRECEDING)
      .map(hourOf),
  };
};

describe("AvailableTimes with a partial-day out-of-office window", () => {
  afterEach(() => {

    bookerTime.timezone = "UTC";
  });

  it("renders the slots before the window, one away panel, then the slots after it", () => {
    renderDay(dayWith([14, 15]));

    const panel = screen.getByText("ooo_user_is_ooo:Host");
    expect(screen.getAllByText("ooo_user_is_ooo:Host")).toHaveLength(1);
    expect(hoursAround(panel)).toEqual({ before: [9, 10, 11, 12, 13], after: [16] });
    expect(screen.queryByText("14:00")).toBeNull();
    expect(screen.queryByText("15:00")).toBeNull();
  });

  it("puts the panel first for a window at the start of the day", () => {
    renderDay(dayWith([9, 10]));

    expect(hoursAround(screen.getByText("ooo_user_is_ooo:Host"))).toEqual({
      before: [],
      after: [11, 12, 13, 14, 15, 16],
    });
  });

  it("puts the panel last for a window at the end of the day", () => {
    renderDay(dayWith([15, 16]));

    expect(hoursAround(screen.getByText("ooo_user_is_ooo:Host"))).toEqual({
      before: [9, 10, 11, 12, 13, 14],
      after: [],
    });
  });

  it("renders one panel per window when a day has two", () => {
    const slots = dayWith([10]).map((slot) =>
      slot.time.startsWith("2026-10-08T14") ? { ...slot, away: true, ...host, emoji: "🦷" } : slot
    );
    renderDay(slots);

    expect(screen.getAllByText("ooo_user_is_ooo:Host")).toHaveLength(2);
    expect(hoursAround(screen.getByText("🩺"))).toEqual({ before: [9], after: [11, 12, 13, 15, 16] });
    expect(hoursAround(screen.getByText("🦷"))).toEqual({ before: [9, 11, 12, 13], after: [15, 16] });
  });
```

```text
import dayjs from "@calcom/dayjs";
import { useBookerStoreContext } from "@calcom/features/bookings/Booker/BookerStoreProvider";
import { getQueryParam } from "@calcom/features/bookings/Booker/utils/query-param";
import type { BookerEvent } from "@calcom/features/bookings/types";
import { PUBLIC_INVALIDATE_AVAILABLE_SLOTS_ON_BOOKING_FORM } from "@calcom/lib/constants";
import { localStorage } from "@calcom/lib/webstorage";
import { BookerLayouts } from "@calcom/prisma/zod-utils";
import classNames from "@calcom/ui/classNames";
import {
  AvailableTimes,
  AvailableTimesSkeleton,
} from "@calcom/web/modules/bookings/components/AvailableTimes";
import { AvailableTimesHeader } from "@calcom/web/modules/bookings/components/AvailableTimesHeader";
import { useWaitlistBookedTimes } from "@calcom/web/modules/bookings/hooks/useWaitlistBookedTimes";
import type { useScheduleForEventReturnType } from "@calcom/web/modules/schedules/hooks/useEvent";
import { useNonEmptyScheduleDays } from "@calcom/web/modules/schedules/hooks/useNonEmptyScheduleDays";
import { useSlotsForAvailableDates } from "@calcom/web/modules/schedules/hooks/useSlotsForDate";
import { useCallback, useMemo, useRef } from "react";
import type { Slot } from "~/schedules/lib/types";
import type { IUseBookingLoadingStates } from "../hooks/useBookings";
import { dayPrintsNoTimes } from "../lib/formatAwayWindow";

type AvailableTimeSlotsProps = {
  extraDays?: number;
  limitHeight?: boolean;
  schedule?: useScheduleForEventReturnType;
  isLoading: boolean;
  seatsPerTimeSlot?: number | null;
  showAvailableSeatsCount?: boolean | null;
  event: {
    data?: Pick<BookerEvent, "length" | "bookingFields" | "price" | "currency" | "metadata"> | null;
  };
  customClassNames?: {
    availableTimeSlotsContainer?: string;
    availableTimeSlotsTitle?: string;
    availableTimeSlotsHeaderContainer?: string;
    availableTimeSlotsTimeFormatToggle?: string;
    availableTimes?: string;
  };
  confirmStepClassNames?: {
    confirmButton?: string;
  };
  loadingStates: IUseBookingLoadingStates;
  isVerificationCodeSending: boolean;
  renderConfirmNotVerifyEmailButtonCond: boolean;
  onSubmit: (timeSlot?: string) => void;
  skipConfirmStep: boolean;
  shouldRenderCaptcha?: boolean;
  watchedCfToken?: string;
  /**
   * This is the list of time slots that are unavailable to book
   */
  unavailableTimeSlots: string[];
  confirmButtonDisabled?: boolean;
  onAvailableTimeSlotSelect: (time: string) => void;
  hideAvailableTimesHeader?: boolean;
};

/**
 * Renders available time slots for a given date.
 * It will extract the date from the booker store.
 * Next to that you can also pass in the `extraDays` prop, this
 * will also fetch the next `extraDays` days and show multiple days
 * in columns next to each other.
 */

export const AvailableTimeSlots = ({
  extraDays,
  limitHeight,
  showAvailableSeatsCount,
  schedule,
  isLoading,
  customClassNames,
  skipConfirmStep,
  seatsPerTimeSlot,
  onSubmit,
  unavailableTimeSlots,
  confirmButtonDisabled,
  confirmStepClassNames,
  onAvailableTimeSlotSelect,
  hideAvailableTimesHeader = false,
  ...props
}: AvailableTimeSlotsProps) => {
  const selectedDate = useBookerStoreContext((state) => state.selectedDate);
```

```text
import dayjs from "@calcom/dayjs";

type AwaySlot = { away?: boolean; outOfOfficeStart?: string };

/**
 * The start and end of an out-of-office window as the booker reads them: in the booker's time zone and
 * 12-hour or 24-hour format. When the two instants fall on different dates in that zone, each one gets its
 * date, written the way the booker's locale writes it.
 */
export function formatAwayWindow(
  startIso: string,
  endIso: string,
  timeZone: string,
  timeFormat: string,
  locale?: string
): { start: string; end: string } {
  // Day.js is used because the result depends on the zone's offset at each instant, which changes on a DST day.
  const start = dayjs.utc(startIso).tz(timeZone);
  const end = dayjs.utc(endIso).tz(timeZone);

  if (start.format("YYYY-MM-DD") === end.format("YYYY-MM-DD")) {
    return { start: start.format(timeFormat), end: end.format(timeFormat) };
  }

  const date = new Intl.DateTimeFormat(locale, { month: "short", day: "numeric", timeZone });
  return {
    start: `${date.format(start.toDate())}, ${start.format(timeFormat)}`,
    end: `${date.format(end.toDate())}, ${end.format(timeFormat)}`,
  };
}

/** A day prints no clock time when every slot is away and no away panel has hours, as for a whole-day entry. */
export function dayPrintsNoTimes(slots: AwaySlot[]): boolean {
  return slots.length > 0 && slots.every((slot) => slot.away && !slot.outOfOfficeStart);
}
```

```typescript
import { BookerLayouts } from "@calcom/prisma/zod-utils";
import { screen } from "@testing-library/react";
import { describe, expect, it, vi } from "vitest";

import { AvailableTimeSlots } from "./AvailableTimeSlots";

  }),
}));

}));

}));

  AvailableTimes: () => null,
  AvailableTimesSkeleton: () => null,
}));

vi.mock("@calcom/web/modules/bookings/components/AvailableTimesHeader", () => ({
  AvailableTimesHeader: ({ showTimeFormatToggle }: { showTimeFormatToggle?: boolean }) => (
    <div data-testid="header">{showTimeFormatToggle ? "toggle shown" : "toggle hidden"}</div>
  ),
}));

const host = { fromUser: { id: 1, displayName: "Host" } };
const at = (hour: number) => `2026-10-08T${String(hour).padStart(2, "0")}:00:00.000Z`;
const awayWindow = { outOfOfficeStart: at(9), outOfOfficeEnd: at(17) };

const renderHeader = (slots: Slot[], layout: BookerLayouts = BookerLayouts.MONTH_VIEW) => {
  day.slots = slots;
  render(
    <AvailableTimeSlots
      isLoading={false}
      event={{ data: null }}
      loadingStates={{ creatingBooking: false, creatingRecurringBooking: false, creatingInstantBooking: false }}
      isVerificationCodeSending={false}
      renderConfirmNotVerifyEmailButtonCond={false}
      onSubmit={vi.fn()}
      skipConfirmStep={false}
      unavailableTimeSlots={[]}
      onAvailableTimeSlotSelect={vi.fn()}
    />,
    { mockStore: { selectedDate: "2026-10-08", layout } }
  );
  return screen.getByTestId("header").textContent;
};

describe("AvailableTimeSlots time format toggle (issue #130)", () => {
  it("shows the toggle on a day with bookable slots", () => {
    expect(renderHeader([{ time: at(9) }, { time: at(10) }])).toBe("toggle shown");
  });

  it("shows the toggle when the first slot is away and the rest of the day is bookable", () => {
    expect(renderHeader([{ time: at(9), away: true, ...host }, { time: at(10) }])).toBe("toggle shown");
  });

  it("shows the toggle when one window with hours covers every slot, because the panel prints times", () => {
    const slots = [9, 10, 11].map((hour) => ({ time: at(hour), away: true, ...host, ...awayWindow }));
    expect(renderHeader(slots)).toBe("toggle shown");
  });

  it("hides the toggle for a whole-day entry, which prints no times", () => {
    const slots = [9, 10, 11].map((hour) => ({ time: at(hour), away: true, ...host }));
    expect(renderHeader(slots)).toBe("toggle hidden");
  });

  it("hides the toggle in column view, where each slot column has its own", () => {
    expect(renderHeader([{ time: at(9) }, { time: at(10) }], BookerLayouts.COLUMN_VIEW)).toBe("toggle hidden");
  });
});
```

Base directory for this skill: /Users/zachshort/.claude/skills/write-doc

# /write-doc

Write papers and documents that read like a careful human wrote them and that Zach can stand behind claim by claim. The rules live in `~/.claude/rules/writing-style.md`. This skill loads them, checks where every claim comes from, drafts, reviews the draft, checks its sources, and checks the saved file.

This skill covers written work only. Chat replies to Zach follow the ASD-STE100 rule in `language-style.md` and nothing else.

## Steps

1. **Load the rules.** Read `~/.claude/rules/writing-style.md` in full before you write anything. Do not work from memory of it.

2. **Fix the brief.** Confirm these four items from the request. Ask one short question only for an item that is missing and cannot be inferred. If step 4 will also need Zach, hold the question and ask everything in one message there.
   - Audience and purpose.
   - Format and file type (`.md`, `.tex`, `.docx`, and so on) and where to save it.
   - Length.
   - Sources or material to use. Never invent a source, a statistic or a quote.

   Also collect what Zach has already supplied in the request or the conversation: his notes, facts he observed, his opinions. Step 4 builds on it.

3. **Plan the argument.** Write the main claim and the order of points for yourself. Each paragraph carries one idea and leads to the next. Decide the facts first: names, numbers, dates, causes. Write each claim down, because step 4 labels them.

4. **Check provenance before you draft.** Label each claim in the plan by where it comes from. Draft nothing until every claim has a label.
   - **Source.** A fact, figure, quote or description taken from something you can name and open: a reading, a file, a web page, a dataset, the code itself. Note which source.
   - **Zach.** Something Zach said or wrote: in the request, in this conversation, or in notes and outlines he wrote. Text that another AI session wrote is not Zach's, even when it sits in his files or an outline presents it as his. Treat it as a draft for him to confirm. Git history does not show who wrote a file, so when you cannot tell whether Zach or an AI session wrote something, label its first-hand claims and opinions **Needs Zach**.
   - **Needs Zach.** A claim that only the author can make:
     - A first-hand claim: what the author saw, read, did, tested, measured, attended or experienced. A description of something the author is expected to have examined counts when you cannot examine it yourself, such as a film, a book you do not have, a meeting, an interview, a lab result or a production incident.
     - A position the document states as the author's own: an opinion, a reaction, a verdict, a recommendation, or the main claim of an argument written in the author's voice.
     - Any "I", "my" or "we" sentence about the author's own experience, reasons or thinking.

   The gate fires on the kind of claim, not on whether the brief marked a gap. Most briefs mark nothing. A request to "make it personal" or "add my perspective" does not license invented experience.

   Three cases need care:
   - A fact from a source stays **Source**. A sentence that says the author learned, noticed, saw or believes that fact is **Needs Zach**.
   - In a genre that implies the author examined the thing, such as a review, a reflection or a site report, a cited description from someone else still reads as the author's own observation. Ask Zach to confirm it.
   - When you revise an existing draft, label the claims already in it the same way. A claim does not become Zach's because it survived an earlier draft.

   If any claim is **Needs Zach**, stop and ask for all of them in one message before you draft, together with any question held from step 2. When most of the document needs Zach, as in a reflection or a personal statement, first ask for his notes in his own words, then plan from them and ask only about what is still missing. Quote or paraphrase each planned claim and say what you need: a fact he observed, a yes or no, or his view in a sentence or two. Do not fill the gap from a secondary source and present it as the author's own. A secondary source's description can go in the draft only as that source's, with a citation, and the report must say so.

   When Zach answers:
   - Build each claim from what he said. Keep his meaning and his details. Do not strengthen, widen or add to them.
   - If he hands a position to you ("you pick", "whatever you think is best"), you may write it. Name it in the report as your choice, not his.
   - If he leaves a first-hand item unanswered or says to skip it, cut the claim or leave a visible marker in the draft: `[NEEDS ZACH: what is missing]`. Never write a first-hand claim from a guess.

   If no claim needs Zach, say so in one line and go on. A README or report built from files you can open often needs no questions.

   This step exists because a document under Zach's name must not report what he did not see or state a view he does not hold. Better prose cannot fix that, and good prose hides the defect from the one reader who could catch it.

5. **Draft with flow.** Draft only from claims that passed step 4. Follow the "Register for papers and documents" section. Keep a matter-of-fact voice. Link sentences with cause and consequence. Mix short and longer sentences. Use concrete detail in place of praise or filler. Prefer connected paragraphs over lists.

6. **Review the draft against the rules.** Re-read the whole draft. Check each group below and fix every problem before you save.
   - **Banned patterns:** no em dashes, no contractions, no litotes, no irony.
   - **Banned words and phrases:** scan for every word in the "Banned AI-signal words" section and replace each with a plain word or a direct statement.
   - **Structure:** no `not just X, but Y` device, no reflex groups of three, no participle tails that add fake analysis, no false ranges, no outline-style conclusion, no closing paragraph that restates the text.
   - **Tone:** no promotional language, no claim of significance without evidence, no vague attribution, no reflex praise.
   - **Formatting:** sentence case headings, rare bold, no emojis, no horizontal rules, no bullet list for every topic, no exact-three or exact-five list by default, no markdown leftovers.
   - **Chatbot leftovers:** no offer of more help, no disclaimer, no placeholder text.

7. **Check sources and citations.** Do this before you save.
   - List every source you used while you drafted: readings, files, fetched pages, notes. Each one that supplied a fact, figure, quote or description must appear in the reference list. In a document with no reference list, such as a README, link the source or name the file. Add any that are missing.
   - Each in-text citation must match a reference entry, and each reference entry must be cited in the text.
   - Where you can open the source, check each quotation word for word and each page number and figure against it. Name any you could not check in the report.
   - Each **Needs Zach** claim in the draft must be supplied by Zach, handed to you by him, cut, or marked.

8. **Save the file.** Write or edit the file with the normal tools. For a Word document, use the docx skill, then continue to the next step.

9. **Run the check.** Run this command on the saved file:

   ```bash
   ~/.claude/hooks/no-em-dash.sh check <path-to-file>
   ```

   It checks em dashes, contractions and banned words. It reads `.md`, `.mdx`, `.txt`, `.rst`, `.tex`, `.adoc`, `.docx`, `.doc`, `.rtf` and `.odt` files. If it prints problems, fix them in the file and run it again until it prints `PASS`. The same check also runs automatically after each Write, Edit and Word-file creation, so a failure there is the same failure.

10. **Report to Zach in ASD-STE100.** Give the file path, a one-line summary of what the document says, and any point where you chose between two options. State the provenance: which claims came from Zach, which positions you chose at his request, which gaps are marked or cut, and which descriptions rest on a secondary source. State any claim or quotation you could not verify. Do not paste the document into the chat.

## If you use subagents to write

A subagent may not load the rules files. Paste these into its prompt: the banned patterns, the banned words list, the structural tells list, the flowing register and the labeled claims from step 4. It may use only claims that passed step 4, and it must not add a first-hand claim or a position of its own. Then run steps 6, 7 and 9 yourself on its output.

## Limits to report honestly

- The script catches words, phrases, em dashes and contractions. It cannot catch layout, participle tails or vague attribution. Step 6 covers those, and it depends on your own careful re-read.
- No script checks provenance or citations. Steps 4 and 7 depend on your own labels. When you are not sure whether a claim is first-hand, label it **Needs Zach**.
- The word rules and the hook address what a human reader notices. They do not lower AI-detector scores: a draft that passed them scored 100% AI on GPTZero with no flagged words or patterns. Do not promise Zach a detector result.
- A Word file is checked only when the command that made it names the file. A script that writes a `.docx` without its name in the command escapes the automatic check, so always run step 9.

```text
### Not tested automatically, and why

- **How the panel reads in the browser.** The unit tests check the text and the order of the panels, not the spacing or the look of two panels in one day. This needs a manual walk with two back-to-back entries and the booking page set to another time zone.
- **The toggle in `AvailableTimeSlots`.** The rule is a pure function (`dayPrintsNoTimes`) with its own tests. The one line that passes its result to `AvailableTimesHeader` is not rendered in a test, because `AvailableTimeSlots` needs the booker store, the schedule query and the waitlist hook.
- **The locale passed to the formatter.** `AvailableTimes.tsx` passes `i18n.language` to `formatAwayWindow`. The test mock always returns `en`, so a wrong locale source would still pass. The formatter's own tests cover `en`, `en-GB` and `de`.
- **The join from a stored entry to the slot fields.** The engine tests start from windows built by hand, and the formatter tests start from ISO instants. No single unit test goes from an entry stored in the host's zone through `getUserAvailability` to the slot fields. The join (`getUserAvailability.ts:828-832`) was read, and the manual walk in two zones checks it.
- **API v2 responses.** The API v2 suites need a database and did not run here. The claim for `2024-09-04` (away slots filtered) and for `2024-04-15` (slots returned unchanged) comes from reading `slots-output.service.ts` in each version, as the review on #130 did.
- **End-to-end booking of an away slot.** No E2E run. The booking path is unchanged by this PR; only optional fields were added to the slot data.

### AI-written tests

All 37 new tests in this PR were written by an AI agent (Claude): 5 in `slots.test.ts`, 20 in `formatAwayWindow.test.ts` and 12 in `AvailableTimes.test.tsx`. They were written before the code they cover, and the 4 engine tests and 10 component tests that depend on the new behavior were run and seen to fail first. The expected values were worked out by hand from the criteria and from UTC offsets, and the working is in comments beside the cases. The harness changes in `AvailableTimes.test.tsx` (a `useBookerTime` mock that a test can change, and a `t` mock that prints the English `ooo_away_window` string) are also AI-written.
```

````text
=== 104-zach-short.md
# Issue #104 -- Show the away badge and redirect for partial-day out-of-office entries

## Class Diagram

![Class diagram](104-zach-short-class.png)

## Sequence Diagram

![Sequence diagram](104-zach-short-sequence.png)

## Q&A

**Class diagram:**

1. Among all the classes shown in the diagram, which 1--2 are most central to understanding the codebase and solving the issue? Explain what role each one plays.

The two most central pieces are `UserAvailabilityService` and the `slots.ts` module.

`UserAvailabilityService` in `packages/features/availability/lib/getUserAvailability.ts` decides what a host's day looks like. Its `_getUserAvailability` method loads the out-of-office entries, calls `getPartialDayOutOfOfficeWindows` from `date-ranges.ts`, and builds the per-day away map in `calculateOutOfOfficeRanges`. It also produces two sets of ranges: `dateRanges`, which still contain a partial-day window, and `oooExcludedDateRanges`, which do not. That split is the reason the feature works, because the booker generates slots from the first set while the booking guard checks the second.

The `slots.ts` module in `packages/features/schedules/lib` turns ranges into slots. `buildSlotsWithDateRanges` now asks the new `findOutOfOfficeForSlot` helper whether each slot is away. A date with no `windows` is away all day, as before. A date with `windows` marks a slot away only when it overlaps one of them. Without this step the booker would show the window's slots as bookable.

2. What is the most significant relationship shown in the diagram? Explain what it represents in the system and why it matters for understanding the solution.

The most significant relationship is the composition between `IOutOfOfficeData` and `IOutOfOfficeWindow`, together with the inheritance from `IOutOfOfficeWindow` to `IOutOfOfficeEntryData`.

`IOutOfOfficeData` is the away map keyed by host-zone date. Before #104 each date held one record and meant "away all day". Now a date record can own an optional `windows` list, and each window carries its UTC `start` and `end` plus every field of `IOutOfOfficeEntryData` (`fromUser`, `toUser`, `reason`, `emoji`, `notes`). Because a window extends the entry data, the slot engine can copy the matching window onto a slot with the same code that copies a whole-day record, and the booker reads both the same way.

This shape matters because it is additive. A date without `windows` is exactly what it was, so the readers that only know whole days (`DatePicker`, `useNonEmptyScheduleDays`, the weekly view) did not change. The PR body lists the two rejected shapes: a separate map next to `datesOutOfOffice`, and one record per window in place of the date record.

3. Looking back at your implementation, is there anything in this design you would change, and why?

I would change two small things. First, `getPartialDayOutOfOfficeRanges` in `date-ranges.ts` now has no caller outside `date-ranges.test.ts`. `_getUserAvailability` maps the result of `getPartialDayOutOfOfficeWindows` itself, so the old helper is a thin wrapper kept only for its tests. I would remove it and move those test cases onto the new function.

Second, a date record with windows copies the first window's data to the top level so that whole-day readers keep working. That is convenient, but a reader that forgets to check `windows` will treat a partial day as a whole day without any error. A clearer type, for example a discriminated union with a `kind` field, would make the compiler catch that case.

I would also add `notes` to `SlotInfo` in `packages/features/calendars/lib/types.ts`. The server already sends it and the panel already shows it, but the new booker test has to widen the type locally. I left it alone to keep the PR focused.

**Sequence diagram:**

1. What user action or system event starts the sequence, and what is the expected outcome when it completes successfully?

The sequence starts when an attendee opens the host's public booking page (`/pro/30min` in the walk) and selects a date that has a partial-day out-of-office entry, for example 2:00pm to 4:00pm. The booker's `useSchedule` hook calls the `viewer.slots.getSchedule` tRPC procedure, which runs `AvailableSlotsService.getAvailableSlots`.

When it completes, the attendee sees the bookable slots before the window (9:00am to 1:30pm), then one away panel, then the slots after the window (4:00pm and 4:30pm). The panel shows the reason emoji, the "is OOO" line and the public note, which is the same panel a whole-day entry already had. The slots inside the window, and any slot that straddles the leave time, are hidden behind the panel and cannot be booked.

If the entry has a forward user (`toUserId`), the panel also shows a "Book with" button. Clicking it calls `router.push` in `OutOfOfficeInSlots` and opens the forward user's booking page on the same month and date. In the walk this was `/free?month=2026-10&date=2026-10-27`.

2. Identify the 2--3 most important steps in the sequence. For each one, describe what is happening and note whether it involves existing code or new/modified code from your solution.

The first important step is building the away map (new and modified code). `getPartialDayOutOfOfficeWindows` in `date-ranges.ts` is new. It parses each partial-day entry with the DST-safe `wallClockToTimeZone` and lists every date the window touches. `calculateOutOfOfficeRanges` is modified to hang each window under those dates, with a whole-day record winning over a window.

The second step is the range split in `_getUserAvailability` (modified code). The window is no longer subtracted from `dateRanges`, so its slots are generated. It is still subtracted from `oooExcludedDateRanges`, which `ensureAvailableUsers` checks. `buildDateRanges` was also changed to skip windowed dates when it removes whole days.

The third step is slot marking and rendering (new and modified code). In `buildSlotsWithDateRanges`, the new `findOutOfOfficeForSlot` marks a slot away when `slotStart < windowEnd && slotEnd > windowStart`. In the booker, `AvailableTimes` now renders one `OOOSlot` at the first slot of each run of away slots. The panel itself, `OutOfOfficeInSlots`, and its redirect button are existing code.

3. What error cases or alternative paths are not shown in the diagram, and why did you leave them out?

The diagram leaves out several paths. A booking request for a time inside the window goes through `ensureAvailableUsers`, which reads `oooExcludedDateRanges` and throws `NoAvailableUsersFound`. That is the booking flow, not the page view, and the existing guard needed no change.

Team events are also not shown. `getAggregatedAvailability` uses `oooExcludedDateRanges` for collective, round-robin and multi-host events, so the window is removed before `getSlots` runs and no panel appears. That behaviour is unchanged from PR #85.

Other paths left out are the slot cache in `withSlotsCache`, a holiday on the same date (it replaces the windows), a window that crosses midnight (it appears under both dates), the DST change day, and the platform atoms, where `OOOSlot` renders nothing. API v2 also drops away slots in `slots-output.service.ts`, so its responses do not change. These are covered by unit tests or do not change the main flow, and showing all of them would hide the main path.

**Cross-cutting:**

4. If you used AI to create or check any part of the diagrams, describe what it produced, what you verified against the actual code, and what you had to correct or add. If AI was not used, write "N/A."

The diagrams were drafted with Claude Code from the diff of branch `feat/issue-104-partial-day-ooo-away` and from the PR description I wrote for #104. Claude Code produced the Mermaid source for both diagrams, the stereotypes that mark new, modified and existing code, and first drafts of these answers. It was told to check every class, function and file name against the worktree before using it.

I then verified the class relationships against the code. I checked that `IOutOfOfficeWindow` really extends `IOutOfOfficeEntryData`, that `UserAvailabilityService` and `AvailableSlotsService` get their repositories through injected `dependencies`, and that `getAggregatedAvailability` picks `oooExcludedDateRanges` for team events. I also traced the sequence through `getScheduleHandler`, `_getAvailableSlots`, `calculateHostsAndAvailabilities`, `getSlots` and the booker components to confirm the order of calls and which steps are new.
````

```text
Closes #130

## What this does

The away panel for a partial-day out-of-office entry now prints the hours of the entry, for example "Away 9:00am to 10:00am". The hours are in the time zone and the 12-hour or 24-hour format selected on the booking page. Two entries that touch now give two panels. Before this change they gave one panel that showed only the first entry, so the second entry's note and redirect were lost.

## Design

**How the window reaches the panel.** `slots.ts` already copies the entry's data onto each away slot. It now also copies the window's ISO start and end into two optional fields, `outOfOfficeStart` and `outOfOfficeEnd`. Only a window has a `start`, so the fields are set behind a `"start" in` check and the slots of a whole-day entry get neither. `findOutOfOfficeForSlot` now declares that it can return an `IOutOfOfficeWindow`, which is what it returned at runtime already. The date record's top-level copy of the first window (`getUserAvailability.ts`, `acc[date] = { ...entryData, windows: [record] }`) is built from the entry data alone, so it has no `start` and cannot put the fields on another slot.

Two alternatives were rejected in the issue. A per-date list of windows beside the slots adds a new response shape that every consumer must join to the slots. Working out the hours in the booker from the first and last away slot shows slot times, which fails criterion 2.

**Where one panel ends and the next starts.** `AvailableTimes` starts a new panel when the slot's `outOfOfficeStart` or `outOfOfficeEnd` differs from the previous away slot. The same rule decides the all-away layout: when every slot is away for the same window (or for a whole-day entry, where both fields are absent), the day keeps the single whole-day panel. When two windows cover the day, the day goes through the normal list and gets one panel per window. Comparing reason and note was rejected because two entries with the same reason would merge. One panel that lists every window was rejected because a panel has one redirect button.

**The formatter.** `formatAwayWindow(startIso, endIso, timeZone, timeFormat, locale)` in `apps/web/modules/bookings/lib/formatAwayWindow.ts` is a pure function. It uses Day.js for the times because the result depends on the zone's offset at each instant, and it uses the same format strings as the slot buttons (`h:mma`, `HH:mm`). When the two instants are on different dates in the booker's zone, each time gets its date from `Intl.DateTimeFormat` with the booker's locale (month short, day numeric), for example "Oct 8, 22:00" in `en` and "8 Oct, 22:00" in `en-GB`. A window that ends exactly at the booker's midnight counts as two dates, because midnight is the first instant of the next date.

**The 12-hour and 24-hour toggle.** `AvailableTimeSlots` hid the toggle on a day where every slot is away. A day covered by windows now prints hours, so the toggle stays. It is hidden only when every slot is away and no panel has hours (`dayPrintsNoTimes`).

**Types.** `SlotInfo` (`packages/features/calendars/lib/types.ts`) and the booker's slot type (`IGetAvailableSlots` in `useAvailableTimeSlots.ts`, which is the declared return type of the tRPC schedule query) both list `notes`, `outOfOfficeStart` and `outOfOfficeEnd`. `AvailableTimes.test.tsx` no longer widens the type locally.

## Changes from the spec, after the review on #130

- The fields are named `outOfOfficeStart` and `outOfOfficeEnd` (review problem 4).
- Criterion 7 is narrowed. API v2 `2024-09-04` filters away slots out, so its responses do not change. API v2 `2024-04-15` with no `slotFormat` and no `timeZone` returns slots unchanged, so away slots there now carry the two new fields. The fields are optional and additive, which `agents/rules/api-no-breaking-changes.md` allows, so this PR does not strip them (review problem 2).
- Criterion 9 (removing `getPartialDayOutOfOfficeRanges`) is out of this PR. It moved to a separate hardening issue so this PR stays inside the size limit. The function and its tests are unchanged here.
- A window that crosses the attendee's midnight appears on both days with the full hours and the dates. This is now tested (criterion 3).

## Out of scope

- A booked time inside a window splits the window into two panels with the same hours. `mergeByTime` puts the booked time between the away slots. This behavior comes from #104.
- Embeds render `AvailableTimes` (`Embed.tsx:416`), so they show the hours too.
- Team events, a discriminated union for `IOutOfOfficeData`, the platform atoms (their `SlotInfo` is unchanged and `OOOSlot` renders nothing there), the redirect switch in the form, and overlap rules on the server.
- Entries that overlap. Each slot still goes to the first window that matches, and each panel shows its own window's hours, so two ranges can overlap on screen.

## Tech Debt

- The weekly view (`apps/web/modules/calendars/weeklyview/components/event/Empty.tsx`) also renders `OutOfOfficeInSlots` and does not pass the hours. Its panel is unchanged.
- The discrimination between a window and a whole-day record is a `"start" in` check on a union. A discriminated union for `IOutOfOfficeData` would make it explicit, and the issue leaves that out because it changes every reader of the map.
- `getPartialDayOutOfOfficeRanges` still has no caller outside its tests. Its removal is tracked in the separate hardening issue.
- Only `en/common.json` has `ooo_away_window`. Other locales fall back to English until they are translated, and the word order "start to end" is fixed by that string.
- The date beside a time has no weekday and no year. An entry longer than a year would be ambiguous.
- The panel does not name the time zone. The booking page shows the selected zone.
- An entry whose end is set to 23:59 is stored as 23:59:59.999 (`outOfOfficeCreateOrUpdate.handler.ts:42-45`), so the panel prints "to 23:59" (for a New York attendee of a London host, "to 6:59pm"). That matches what the host picked, but no test covers it.
```

```text
  async getOutputSlots(
    availableSlots: TimeSlots,
    duration?: number,
    eventTypeId?: number,
    slotFormat?: SlotFormat,
    timeZone?: string
  ): Promise<TimeSlots | RangeSlots> {
    if (!slotFormat) {
      return timeZone ? this.setTimeZone(availableSlots, timeZone) : availableSlots;
    }

    const formattedSlots = await this.formatSlots(availableSlots, duration, eventTypeId, slotFormat);
    return timeZone ? this.setTimeZoneRange(formattedSlots, timeZone) : formattedSlots;
```

```mmd
    Fmt-->>ATS: false, so the header keeps the 12-hour and 24-hour toggle
    ATS->>AT: render the slots of Oct 8

    Note over AT: Modified. False here, because the day has bookable slots
    loop for each slot (merged with booked times)
        alt slot not away
            AT->>AT: SlotItem
        else previous slot is in the same panel (same window)
            AT->>AT: skip
        else first slot of a run with this window
            AT->>OOO: OOOSlot with this slot's entry data and window
            Note over AT,OOO: Modified. The window decides where a panel ends, so the doctor and travel entries give two panels
        end
    end

    loop for each OOOSlot (doctor, then travel)
        OOO->>OOO: useBookerTime() gives timezone and timeFormat, useLocale() gives i18n.language
        OOO->>Fmt: formatAwayWindow(outOfOfficeStart, outOfOfficeEnd, timezone, timeFormat, language)
        Note over OOO,Fmt: New. Day.js converts each instant to the booker's zone. A date is added to each time only when the two instants fall on different dates there
        Fmt-->>OOO: {start: "2:00pm", end: "3:00pm"} for a London attendee
        OOO->>Panel: render with awayWindow, notes, toUser
        Panel-->>Attendee: panel: emoji, "Host is OOO", "Away 2:00pm to 3:00pm", the public note, "Book with" button
        Note over OOO,Panel: Modified. One new line under the is-OOO line, from the ooo_away_window string
    end

    opt attendee changes the time format or the zone
        Attendee->>Booker: toggle 12-hour or 24-hour, or pick another zone
        Booker->>OOO: re-render with the new useBookerTime values
        OOO->>Fmt: formatAwayWindow with the new zone or format
        Fmt-->>OOO: for example {start: "14:00", end: "15:00"}
        OOO->>Panel: render with the new awayWindow
        Panel-->>Attendee: "Away 14:00 to 15:00"
    end
```

```markdown
# Issue #130 -- Show the hours of a partial-day out-of-office window on the away panel

## Class Diagram

![Class diagram](130-zach-short-class.png)

## Sequence Diagram

![Sequence diagram](130-zach-short-sequence.png)

## Q&A

**Class diagram:**

1. Among all the classes shown in the diagram, which 1--2 are most central to understanding the codebase and solving the issue? Explain what role each one plays.

The two most central pieces are the `slots.ts` module and the `AvailableTimes` component.

`slots.ts` in `packages/features/schedules/lib` is where a slot learns which window marks it. Since #104, `buildSlotsWithDateRanges` asks `findOutOfOfficeForSlot` for the record that covers each slot, and that record is either a whole-day entry or one `IOutOfOfficeWindow`. For #130 the module copies the window's `start` and `end` onto the slot as `outOfOfficeStart` and `outOfOfficeEnd`. It does this only when the record has a `start`, so the slots of a whole-day entry carry no hours. Every later step reads these two fields, so without this step the booker would have nothing to print.

`AvailableTimes` in `apps/web/modules/bookings/components` decides how many panels a day gets and where they sit. Its new `inSamePanel` check treats two away slots as one panel only when both window fields match. That one rule fixes the bug from #104, where two entries that touch were drawn as one panel and the second entry's note and redirect were lost. The same check also decides the whole-day layout, so a day with one window over every slot keeps the single panel.

2. What is the most significant relationship shown in the diagram? Explain what it represents in the system and why it matters for understanding the solution.

The most significant relationship is the chain from `slots.ts` to `SlotInfo`, then over tRPC to the booker's `Slot`, and from `OOOSlot` to `formatAwayWindow.ts`.

The server sends instants, not text. `slots.ts` puts two UTC ISO strings on each away slot, and `SlotInfo` and the booker's `IGetAvailableSlots` type both declare them as optional fields. The booker then turns them into text in `OOOSlot`, which reads the attendee's zone and 12-hour or 24-hour choice from `useBookerTime` and calls the pure `formatAwayWindow`. Because the conversion happens at render time, a change of zone or format on the booking page updates the hours the same way it updates the slot buttons.

This split matters for two reasons. The fields are additive, so the readers that do not know about them, including API v2 `2024-04-15`, keep working. And the formatter has no React or tRPC in it, so its time zone, DST and midnight cases are tested with plain inputs.

3. Looking back at your implementation, is there anything in this design you would change, and why?

I would change four things.

First, a slot learns that its record is a window through a `"start" in` check on a union type. A discriminated union for `IOutOfOfficeData`, with a field that names the kind of record, would let the compiler catch a reader that treats a window as a whole day. I left it out because it changes every reader of the map.

Second, the weekly view (`apps/web/modules/calendars/weeklyview/components/event/Empty.tsx`) also renders `OutOfOfficeInSlots`, but it does not pass the hours. Its panel still shows no times, so the two views now disagree.

Third, the redirect date comes from the panel's slot through `dayjs(time).format("YYYY-MM-DD")`, not from the day column the attendee is looking at. The mutation run for #130 showed that this date depends on which slot of a run gets the panel, and a run that crosses midnight UTC can send the attendee to the next day. I would pass the column's date to the panel.

Fourth, `getPartialDayOutOfOfficeRanges` in `date-ranges.ts` still has no caller outside its tests. I would remove it. That removal now has its own issue so this PR stays inside the size limit.

**Sequence diagram:**

1. What user action or system event starts the sequence, and what is the expected outcome when it completes successfully?

The sequence starts when an attendee opens a host's booking page and picks a date with a partial-day out-of-office entry. The diagram uses the user scenario of #130: a London host is away from 2:00pm to 3:00pm for the doctor and from 3:00pm to 4:00pm for travel, two entries that touch. The booker's `useSchedule` hook calls `viewer.slots.getSchedule`.

When it completes, the attendee sees two away panels between the bookable slots, one for each entry. Each panel shows its own emoji, note and redirect, and a new line with the window's hours, for example "Away 2:00pm to 3:00pm", in the zone and the 12-hour or 24-hour format selected on the page. The time format toggle stays in the header. If the attendee changes the zone or the format, the hours change with it.

2. Identify the 2--3 most important steps in the sequence. For each one, describe what is happening and note whether it involves existing code or new/modified code from your solution.

The first important step is copying the window onto the slot (modified code). In `buildSlotsWithDateRanges`, a slot that overlaps a window gets `outOfOfficeStart` and `outOfOfficeEnd` from that window. The availability service that builds the windows, and `findOutOfOfficeForSlot` that finds the match, are existing code from #104. Only the return type of `findOutOfOfficeForSlot` changed.

The second step is splitting the day into panels (modified code). `AvailableTimes` walks the slots and starts a new `OOOSlot` at the first slot of each run that shares one window. The doctor slot and the travel slot are both away, but their windows differ, so they get two panels.

The third step is formatting and printing the hours (new code). `OOOSlot` calls `formatAwayWindow` with the slot's window and the attendee's zone, format and locale. `OutOfOfficeInSlots` prints the result with the new `ooo_away_window` string. Before that, `AvailableTimeSlots` calls the new `dayPrintsNoTimes` to decide whether the header keeps the toggle.

3. What error cases or alternative paths are not shown in the diagram, and why did you leave them out?

The diagram leaves out several paths. A whole-day entry and a holiday give slots with no window fields, so their panels print no hours. That path is the same as before #130. A window that covers every slot of the day keeps the single whole-day panel and adds its hours. A window that crosses the attendee's midnight shows on both days, with a date beside each time.

Other paths left out are a booked time inside a window, which splits it into two panels with the same hours (behavior from #104), team events, which never show the panel, embeds, which render the same component, and API v2. The `2024-04-15` version returns the two new fields unchanged and the `2024-09-04` version filters away slots out. These are covered by unit tests or do not change the main flow, and showing all of them would hide the main path.

**Cross-cutting:**

4. If you used AI to create or check any part of the diagrams, describe what it produced, what you verified against the actual code, and what you had to correct or add. If AI was not used, write "N/A."

The diagrams were drafted with Claude Code from the diff of PR #153 and its description. Claude Code wrote the Mermaid source for both diagrams in the same style as my #104 diagrams, with stereotypes for new, modified and existing code, and wrote first drafts of these answers. It checked the class, function, file and string names against the code before using them, and it rendered the PNGs with mermaid-cli. While rendering, it fixed two problems in its own output: Mermaid cut a note at a `#` character, and it printed `{{start}}` wrongly.

I read both diagrams and checked that the classes, the arrows and the order of calls match the code. I also read these answers and agree with them.

```
